People here don't seem to understand what a trademark is. It doesn't prevent you from using these words in this combination in regular speech. It prevents you from using that combination of words and associating them with a product or service, particularly if it is perceived to devalue the trademark holder's associated identity, product, or service.

This is why the World Wrestling Federation (WWF) was forced to change its name in a dispute with the World Wildlife Foundation. Trademarking common English phrases or words to identify a common industry practice, and there are hundreds of examples to draw from to show how this is generally not harmful to the public.

Having a trademark doesn't prevent people from using that combination of words in speech. It also doesn't prevent fair use. I mean, Nike trademarked "Just do it", but that wouldn't give them license to go after Shia Labouf.
